We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., a single reaction) from commercially available precursors, total cost <= $250. The target SMILES is a complex molecule: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Let's decode: It's an alkene attached to phenyl (styrene) and a cyclobutane? Actually C@@H1[CH2][CH2][CH2][C@@]1(OH)C(F)(F)F? Wait there is CF3 attached to carbon 15? Actually C:15 with three Fs (F16,F17,F18) is CF3 group attached to the cyclobutane? The structure: a cyclobutane ring (C9-10-11-12-13) with OH on C13 and CF3 on C15? Wait C15 is attached to C13? The SMILES: ...[C@@H]1[CH2][CH2][CH2][C@@]1([OH])C(F)(F)F. So it's a cyclobutane with a CF3 substituent on the bridge carbon (C13) and OH also on same carbon? Actually C@@:13 has both OH and CF3? The SMILES: [C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] - So carbon 13 is attached to OH and also attached to carbon 15 which is CF3? Wait carbon 15 is attached to three Fs, but carbon 13 is attached to carbon 15 (CF3). So the cyclobutane carbon 13 is attached to a CF3 group and OH.

Thus target is a CF3-substituted cyclobutanol with a styrene side chain.

We need a single-step retrosynthesis: maybe from a precursor that already has CF3 and OH? The template we found (149288) seems to be a reaction that forms CF3 from a gem-difluoro-chloride? The template appears to be a halogen exchange? The retro template: [C:3]-[C;H0;D4;+0:2](-[F;D1;H0:4])(-[F;D1;H0:5])-[F;H0;D1;+0:1]>>C=C(-F)-[F;H0;D1;+0:1].Cl-[C;H0;D4;+0:2](-[C:3])(-[F;D1;H0:4])-[F;D1;H0:5]

Hard to parse. The forward reaction (retro direction) seems to break a C-C bond between a CF3 carbon and a carbon bearing two Fs? Actually the product side is a CF3 attached to carbon, and the reactant side includes C=C(F)F (gem-difluoro alkene) and a chlorinated carbon attached to CF3? The apply_template gave two precursors: "C=C(F)F" and "C=C(c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1CCC[C@@]1(O)C(F)(F)Cl". So the retrosynthetic step suggests that our target can be made from gem-difluoroethylene (C=C(F)F) and a chlorinated cyclobutanol with difluoro? Actually the second precursor is a cyclobutanol with a C(F)(F)Cl substituent (i.e., a gem-difluoro-chloride). The reaction likely is a halogen exchange to form CF3.

Thus we have two precursors: 1) C=C(F)F (gem-difluoroethylene) which is commercially available? Likely yes, maybe cheap. 2) C=C(c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1CCC[C@@]1(O)C(F)(F)Cl (a cyclobutanol with gem-difluoro-chloride and styrene). That second precursor is likely not commercially available (complex). So not good.

We need a different retrosynthesis: maybe directly purchase the target? But target is not commercially available (likely not). Need a single-step from two cheap precursors.

Alternative: Use a trifluoromethylation reaction: e.g., addition of CF3 radical to an alkene. Starting from the same alkene without CF3: the precursor could be the same cyclobutanol with a double bond (i.e., C=C(c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1CCC[C@@]1(O)C(H)(H)?? Actually we need a precursor lacking CF3 but having a hydrogen that can be replaced by CF3 via radical addition. The template for trifluoromethylation may exist.

Search for templates forming CF3 from a C-H bond (trifluoromethylation). Let's search functional_groups_formed: trifluoromethyl, functional_groups_broken maybe none.
